title: Ἔλαφος καὶ λέων ⟨ἐν σπηλαίῳ⟩
titleEn: The Deer and the Lion in the Cave
part: The Deer and the Lion in the Cave (Chambry 104 · Perry 76)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 104 (= Perry 76). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », ⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔλαφος κυνηγοὺς φεύγουσα ἐγένετο κατά τι σπήλαιον, ἐν ᾧ λέων ἦν, καὶ ἐνταῦθα εἰσῄει κρυβησομένη.
sentences.tr: Elaphos kynēgous pheugousa egeneto kata ti spēlaion, en hōi leōn ēn, kai entautha eisēiei krybēsomenē.
sentences.l: A deer, fleeing hunters, came to a certain cave, in which there was a lion, and went in there to hide.
sentences.n: The title's ⟨ἐν σπηλαίῳ⟩ is in angle brackets because Chambry supplies it — presumably to tell this deer apart from the one in the vine and the one on the shore. ἐγένετο κατά with the accusative is the fables' regular 'came to be over against, arrived at' a place. κρυβησομένη is a future participle expressing purpose: she went in in order to hide.

sentences.t: Συλληφθεῖσα δὲ ὑπὸ τοῦ λέοντος καὶ ἀναιρουμένη ἔφη· « Βαρυδαίμων ἔγωγε, ἥτις ἀνθρώπους φεύγουσα ἐμαυτὴν θηρίῳ ἐνεχείρισα. »
sentences.tr: Syllēphtheisa de hypo tou leontos kai anairoumenē ephē· « Barydaimōn egōge, hētis anthrōpous pheugousa emautēn thēriōi enecheirisa. »
sentences.l: And having been seized by the lion and being made away with, she said: « Ill-fated indeed am I, who, fleeing men, put myself into a beast's hands. »
sentences.i: And as the lion seized her and was making an end of her she said: « Wretched creature that I am — fleeing men, I have handed myself over to a beast. »
sentences.n: The dying self-address has a fixed shape in these fables: an adjective, ἔγωγε, then ἥτις with the reason — 'wretched I, who am the sort to have done this'. βαρυδαίμων is 'heavy in one's daimōn', weighed down by the lot assigned one. ἐγχειρίζω is literally 'to put into the hand', and the hands here are a lion's.

sentences.t: Οὕτως ἔνιοι τῶν ἀνθρώπων διὰ φόβον ἐλάττονος εἰς κίνδυνον μείζονα ἑαυτοὺς ἐμβάλλουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtōs enioi tōn anthrōpōn dia phobon elattonos eis kindynon meizona heautous emballousin.
sentences.l: So some men, through fear of a lesser thing, throw themselves into a greater danger.
sentences.n: ἐλάττονος is a bare genitive after φόβον, with κινδύνου most likely understood from the μείζονα κίνδυνον that answers it: fear of the smaller danger, flight into the larger.
